paper.title: Regret Lower Bound and Optimal Algorithm in Dueling Bandit Problem

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed dueling bandit problem with a Condorcet winner (RMED1, horizonless)
unmapped: Regret per round is (Delta_{1,i}+Delta_{1,j})/2 when pair (i,j) is compared (average Condorcet regret)
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t=1,2,\dots,T$, the forecaster selects a pair of arms $(l(t), m(t)) \in [K]^2$, then receives a relative feedback $\myX{l(t)}{m(t)}(t) \sim \Bernoulli(\muij{l(t)}{m(t)})$ ... Throughout this paper, we will assume that the preference matrix has a Condorcet winner ... We define the regret per round as $r(t) = (\myDelta{1}{i}+\myDelta{1}{j})/2$ when the pair $(i,j)$ is compared.

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed dueling bandit problem with a Condorcet winner (RMED2FH, known horizon)
unmapped: Regret per round is (Delta_{1,i}+Delta_{1,j})/2 when pair (i,j) is compared (average Condorcet regret)
settings.definition_quote: Note that, unlike RMED1 and RMED2, RMED2FH requires the number of rounds $T$ beforehand to conduct the initial $\myalpha \log{\log{T}}$ draws of each pair.

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed dueling bandit, Condorcet model M_C (lower bound)
unmapped: Regret per round is (Delta_{1,i}+Delta_{1,j})/2 when pair (i,j) is compared (average Condorcet regret)
settings.definition_quote: The set of preference matrices which have a Condorcet winner is denoted by $\mcondor$. ... A dueling bandit algorithm is strongly consistent for model $\model \subset \mcondor$ iff it has $\Expect[\Regret(T)] = o(T^a)$ regret for any $a > 0$ and any $\Mat \in \model$.

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed dueling bandit, total-order model M_o (lower bound)
unmapped: Preference matrix induces a total order (i < j iff mu_{i,j} < 1/2), without stochastic transitivity; learner may know the total-order structure
Regret per round is (Delta_{1,i}+Delta_{1,j})/2 when pair (i,j) is compared
settings.definition_quote: We also define the set of preference matrices satisfying the total order by $\morder\subset \mcondor$; that is, the relation $i\prec j\Leftrightarrow \muij{i}{j} < 1/2$ induces a total order iff $\{ \muij{i}{j} \}\in\morder$.

conditions: applies to each suboptimal arm i != 1
algorithm strongly consistent for model M_C (E[R(T)] = o(T^a) for all a>0)

source.label: lem:drawlower
source.quote: (i) Let an arm $i \in \nonwinner$ and preference matrix $\Mat \in \mcondor$ be arbitrary. Given any strongly consistent algorithm for model $\mcondor$, we have \Expect\{\sum_{j \in \SetO{i}} d(\muij{i}{j}, 1/2) N_{i,j}(T) \} \geq (1 - o(1)) \log{T}

results.notes: Bound on divergence-weighted expected number of comparisons of arm i with its superiors (quantity other). Part (ii) gives the same for total-order model (r2).

conditions: applies to each suboptimal arm i != 1
algorithm strongly consistent for model M_o

source.label: lem:drawlower
source.quote: (ii) Furthermore, inequality \eqref{ineq:drawlower} holds for any $\Mat \in \morder$ given any strongly consistent algorithm for $\morder$.

symbols.c_i: min over superiors j of arm i (mu_{i,j}<1/2) of (Delta_{1,i}+Delta_{1,j})/(2 d(mu_{i,j},1/2)), with Delta_{1,j}=mu_{1,j}-1/2 and d the Bernoulli KL

conditions: algorithm strongly consistent for model M_C

source.label: thm:regretlower
source.quote: (i) Let the preference matrix $\Mat \in \mcondor$ be arbitrary. For any strongly consistent algorithm for model $\mcondor$, \liminf_{T \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\Expect[\Regret(T)]}{\log{T}} \geq \sum_{i \in \nonwinner} \min_{j \in \SetO{i}} \frac{\myDelta{1}{i} + \myDelta{1}{j}}{2 d(\muij{i}{j}, 1/2)} holds.

results.notes: Regret defined through means (Condorcet regret) so pseudo_regret; comparator is the Condorcet winner pair (1,1).

symbols.c_i: min over superiors j of arm i of (Delta_{1,i}+Delta_{1,j})/(2 d(mu_{i,j},1/2))

conditions: algorithm strongly consistent for model M_o (total order)

source.label: thm:regretlower
source.quote: (ii) Furthermore, inequality \eqref{ineq:regretlower} holds for any $\Mat \in \morder$ given any strongly consistent algorithm for $\morder$.

results.notes: Same lower bound under total order assumption.

bound.expression: sum_subopt(((1 + delta_a)*log(T) + f_K)*Delta_1i/(2*d_i1)) + K**2 + K/delta_a**2 + K*exp(A*K - f_K)
bound.expression_latex: \sum_{i \in \nonwinner} \frac{((1 + \mysmalldelta) \log{T} + f(K) ) \myDelta{1}{i}}{2 d(\muij{i}{1}, 1/2)} + O(K^2) + O\left(\frac{K}{\mysmalldelta^2}\right) + O(K \e^{\CoefA K-f(K)})

symbols.f_K: non-negative function f(K) used in the candidate condition of RMED
symbols.Delta_1i: mu_{1,i} - 1/2, margin by which Condorcet winner beats arm i
symbols.A: instance-dependent constant A({mu_ij}) independent of T

conditions: preference matrix has a Condorcet winner (arm 1)

source.label: thm:verone
source.quote: For any sufficiently small $\mysmalldelta > 0$, the regret of RMED1 is bounded as: \Expect[\Regret(T)] \leq \sum_{i \in \nonwinner} \frac{((1 + \mysmalldelta) \log{T} + f(K) ) \myDelta{1}{i}}{2 d(\muij{i}{1}, 1/2)} + O(K^2) + O\left(\frac{K}{\mysmalldelta^2}\right) + O(K \e^{\CoefA K-f(K)})

results.notes: Leading term is explicit; O applies to remaining terms. RMED1 is horizonless.

conditions: preference matrix has a Condorcet winner (arm 1)
tuning: f(K) = c K^{1+eps_alg} for arbitrary c, eps_alg > 0

source.label: thm:verone
source.quote: Therefore, by letting $\mysmalldelta = \log^{-1/3}{T}$ and choosing an $f(K) = c K^{1+\mysmallepsilon}$ for arbitrary $c,\mysmallepsilon>0$, we obtain \Expect[\Regret(T)] \leq \sum_{i \in \nonwinner} \frac{ \myDelta{1}{i} \log{T}}{2 d(\muij{i}{1}, 1/2)} + O(K^{2+\mysmallepsilon}) + O(K\log^{2/3}{T}).

results.notes: Matches lower bound when b*(i)=1 for all i. Leading term explicit constant; O on lower-order terms. delta is an analysis parameter, so the algorithm remains horizonless.

bound.expression: sum_subopt((Delta_1i + Delta_1b_i)*(1 + delta_a)*log(T)/(2*d_ib_i)) + alpha_r*K**2*log(log(T)) + K*exp(A*K - f_K) + K*log(T)/log(log(T)) + K/delta_a**2 + K*f_K
bound.expression_latex: \sum_{i \in \nonwinner} \frac{(\myDelta{1}{i} + \myDelta{1}{\bsi}) ((1 + \mysmalldelta) \log{T})}{2d(\muij{i}{\bsi}, 1/2)} + O(\myalpha K^2 \log{\log{T}}) + O(K \e^{\CoefA K - f(K)}) + O\left( \frac{K \log{T}}{\log{\log{T}}} \right) + O\left(\frac{K}{\mysmalldelta^2}\right) + O\left(Kf(K)\right)

symbols.alpha_r: RMED2FH exploration parameter alpha > 0 (each pair drawn ceil(alpha log log T) times initially)
symbols.Delta_1b_i: mu_{1,b*(i)} - 1/2 where b*(i) is the superior of i minimizing (Delta_{1,i}+Delta_{1,j})/d(mu_{i,j},1/2)
symbols.A: instance-dependent constant A({mu_ij}) > 0 independent of T

conditions: preference matrix has a Condorcet winner (arm 1)
b*(i) assumed unique (paper says extendable to ties)

source.label: thm:vertwo
source.quote: For any sufficiently small $\mysmalldelta>0$, the regret of RMED2FH is bounded as: \Expect[\Regret(T)] \leq \sum_{i \in \nonwinner} \frac{(\myDelta{1}{i} + \myDelta{1}{\bsi}) ((1 + \mysmalldelta) \log{T})}{2d(\muij{i}{\bsi}, 1/2)} + O(\myalpha K^2 \log{\log{T}}) + O(K \e^{\CoefA K - f(K)}) + O( \frac{K \log{T}}{\log{\log{T}}} ) + O(\frac{K}{\mysmalldelta^2}) + O(Kf(K))

results.notes: Leading term explicit; O on remaining terms.

bound.expression: sum_subopt((Delta_1i + Delta_1b_i)*log(T)/(2*d_ib_i)) + alpha_r*K**2*log(log(T)) + K*log(T)/log(log(T)) + K**(2 + eps_alg)

conditions: preference matrix has a Condorcet winner (arm 1)

source.label: thm:vertwo
source.quote: By setting $\mysmalldelta = O((\log{T})^{-1/3})$ and choosing an $f(K) = c K^{1+\mysmallepsilon}$ ($c,\mysmallepsilon>0$) we obtain \Expect[\Regret(T)] \leq \sum_{i \in \nonwinner} \frac{(\myDelta{1}{i} + \myDelta{1}{\bsi}) \log{T}}{2d(\muij{i}{\bsi}, 1/2)} + O(\myalpha K^2 \log{\log{T}}) + O( \frac{K  \log{T}}{\log{\log{T}}} )+ O( K^{2+\mysmallepsilon}).

results.notes: Leading term matches the asymptotic lower bound of thm:regretlower (asymptotically optimal).
